title: Normalize contrast ramp & keyboard affordances for mini-charts and dense-table controls (VPAT annex)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our compact chart components (mini sparklines, small-area charts, and inline trend widgets) and dense table action controls have inconsistent contrast tokens and incomplete keyboard affordances. Several customer-reported accessibility issues surfaced during audits: low-contrast overlay tooltips in dark themes, legend items that are not reachable or focus-visible with arrow/Home/End behaviors, and small icon buttons in high-density rows that lack sufficient touch/focus targets and aria-label consistency. Goal: Harmonize the contrast ramp for chart overlays, standardize focus rings and hit targets for dense table controls, and produce a VPAT annex documenting screen-reader scenarios and test evidence for release. Scope: token remediation for chart overlays and legend pills; keyboard navigation patterns for chart legends (arrow navigation, Home/End, Shift+Tab edge cases); focus/tap target expansion for small table row actions; VPAT evidence package (annotated scenarios, recordings, test matrix). Out of scope: full component redesign, canvas-level rendering engine changes, and platform-engine kernel work (will coordinate with ENG for follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Contrast tokens: Overlay/background and tooltip text meet WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1) and 3.0 where applicable for text >= 18pt large text alternative ratio; design token aliases created for dark/light themes
Keyboard: Chart legends support linear arrow navigation (+Left/Right or Up/Down per orientation), Home/End to jump to first/last legend item, and visible focus state consistent with design tokens
Dense table controls: Small icon buttons have 44x44px hit targets and consistent aria-labels; visual focus ring matches token spec
VPAT annex: A single document with 10 annotated scenarios, 3 screen-reader test recordings (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS), and a pass/fail matrix per scenario
Design handoff: Figma specs, token migration sheet, and redlines for engineering with clear fallbacks for older clients
work_items: Audit: run contrast checks across all chart variants and dense table states (hover, focus, active)
Define token set: propose token aliases and migration mapping (old -> new)
Design patterns: keyboard nav spec for horizontal/vertical legend groups and edge cases
Prototype: interactive Figma + small Cypress a11y harness for legend keyboard behavior
VPAT: compile scenarios, record screen-reader tests, and assemble the annex PDF
Handoff: create GH issue template for ENG work and schedule joint design/eng review
tradeoffs: Token renaming vs aliasing: renaming reduces confusion long-term but increases breaking risk; propose alias approach with deprecation timeline
Hit target expansion may increase row density complaints; recommend opt-in compact mode with explicit tokens
Enforcing Home/End semantics requires adding tabindex and keyboard handlers on legend list items; small JS shim has minimal perf cost but needs ENG review
